decisions.decision: docs/glossary.md stays constitution-plane; the ENFORCEMENT was brought up to ADR-0001, not the other way round
decisions.rationale: ADR-0001:48 is accepted and unsuperseded. Two Claude audits recommended the opposite repair by citing ADR-0010, which was still Status: proposed. An unratified record cannot override a ratified one. codex sol (medium) caught the inversion

decisions.decision: Constitution ownership and review obligation are ORTHOGONAL and this is now written into three surfaces
decisions.rationale: Ownership controls WHO MAY EDIT; a binding controls WHEN A HUMAN OWES A REVIEW. contract-graph-adr-0009 already pairs a docs/adr/** target the same way — a counterexample that was in the same registry and had already been read when the wrong recommendation was made

decisions.decision: The glossary is a LITERAL path everywhere, never docs/**
decisions.rationale: A broad glob would deny the whole human-doc tree and still satisfy every glossary row. Negative controls in three modules go red if someone 'fixes' it that way

decisions.decision: Did NOT enable 'Require review from Code Owners' on main; required the `gate` status check instead
decisions.rationale: Solo repo: the sole code owner is also the PR author, GitHub forbids self-approval, and it would need an admin waiver per merge. .github/CODEOWNERS:14-19 recorded that trap. The machine half is enforceable without ceremony; the human half is already enforced in-session by the ledger/contract/golden hooks

decisions.decision: Refused to author the ledger or ratify ADR-0010, three times, including via bash and via delegating to another agent
decisions.rationale: bash WOULD have worked — the hooks bind tool calls, not shells. That is exactly why the rule is about holding it rather than being stopped by it. ledger_guard honours NO token, unlike contract_guard which has HARNESS_DEV_BYPASS; Phase 28 removed that door deliberately. A self-blessed row and an honest seed row are byte-identical, so the committing hand is the only record

context_notes: The defect that dominated this session is the one this repo keeps rediscovering, but in a new shape: not a control that ships green while bypassable, but a control that was never built while four documents said it was. docs/glossary.md was agent-writable for two weeks. The tell was that the DOCUMENTS were right and the CODE was wrong — the opposite of the usual direction, which is why two audits nearly repaired it backwards by deleting the true sentence. Check ADR status fields before citing one as authority: accepted beats proposed, and I used a proposed record as if it were binding. Second lesson, on delegation: I spawned parallel extraction agents, got impatient when they were slow, read the artifacts myself by grep, and committed. That direct read was wrong in three places and the late-arriving delegate caught all three — all three errors made a phase look greener than it was. Grep summaries of PLAN files miss `<task type="checkpoint:human-verify">` declarations. Read task type declarations directly or wait for the delegate. Third: terra's plan ordered A->B->C->ADR->ledger and I did not know why until the end — repointing a binding BEFORE the first ledger exists avoids the amber cycle entirely, because first_seen-unratified compares against the previous COMMITTED ledger and there was none. Trust a plan's ordering even when its reason is not stated. Mechanical: `git commit -- <paths>` puts -m BEFORE the -- or git reads the message as a pathspec; I gave the user a broken command from this exact mistake.
